assertions.title: Entries in the frozen catalogue extract

assertions.note: Tested in both directions: no label without a path under its repository, and no path under a repository without its label. Bare `docs/` paths never occur without a `meridian-runtime/` path in the same entry (0 exceptions), which is why they are counted to that repository rather than to this one. Violations: none

assertions.note: These are the only entries whose evidence this practice can hold as ground truth. They span 24 distinct files and 103 entry-file pairs.
assertions.title: Entries labelled `field`

assertions.note: 103 of 103 pairs resolve: the file exists at 58d9c4c AND the entry's own identifier occurs in its text. Under a stricter reading, where the identifier must also share a line with a scheme name or a URL, 103 of 103 still resolve — reported so the looseness of the rule is visible rather than hidden. Residue: none
assertions.title: Unresolved entry-file pairs at the pinned commit

assertions.note: Searched all 381 files tracked at 58d9c4c for a `corpora/` path segment or a file named `citations.manifest.json` — the evidence form the seed of 2026-07-28 addresses to this practice as "eure Zitationsmanifeste". Neither is present. What this establishes is where the files are NOT; it does not by itself establish who writes the repository where they are.
assertions.title: Files in this repository matching the evidence form attributed to it

assertions.note: 138 entries carry that label. Exactly 1 of them ALSO carries the `field` label and an evidence path in this repository, and is already counted and resolved in A3/A4; the other 137 have no evidence path here at all — their `meridian` evidence lies under `meridian-runtime/` and `docs/`, which this repository does not contain. This audit therefore makes no claim about whether those back-references resolve, only that they cannot be resolved from here.
assertions.title: Entries labelled `meridian` whose evidence is checkable from this repository

assertions.title: Entries labelled `field` whose relevance sentence is a machine judgement

assertions.note: All of them recorded on date(s) ['2026-07-28'], written from ['abstract']. The generative model named in that block is redacted in this practice's freeze and not otherwise reproduced; the unredacted value is in the source file pinned in SOURCES.md.
assertions.title: Entries repository-wide carrying a machine-written relevance sentence

assertions.note: A sieve over all 381 tracked files at 58d9c4c (17 undecodable, skipped): 286 distinct identifier-shaped strings; -7 failing a shape rule (arXiv-shaped year 07-26, month 01-12) leaves 279; -200 occurring only inside instrument 020's vendored third-party register corpus leaves 79; -30 occurring only in synthetic test fixtures leaves 49; of those, 41 are in the catalogue and 8 are not. The large exclusions are the catalogue's, and they are correct: identifiers this practice AUDITED are not identifiers this practice CITES.
assertions.title: Identifier-shaped strings in this repository that the catalogue does not carry

assertions.note: Handed back to the catalogue's keeper as candidates, not as errors: some are sources this practice relies on, some are texts it merely names, and at least one is a defect in this practice's own record rather than a gap in the catalogue (A11). Whether an entry belongs in the catalogue is its keeper's judgement, not this practice's.
assertions.title: The remainder, named

assertions.note: The identifier 10.3030/101135953 is presented as the citation for "EU AI Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, Art. 5.1(d)" in ['journal/2026-07-01.md', 'works/2026-07-01-fairness-trap/work.astro'] — one of which is a SHIPPED work, on its published face. It came out of this audit's own sieve, not out of a reader's complaint. The live fetch that established it does not resolve is an out-of-band observation, recorded with its timestamp in the work's record and deliberately NOT an assertion here: every assertion in this file is offline and reproducible from the pin.
assertions.title: Files in this repository presenting a non-resolving DOI as a citation

caveats.loose_matching: A4's rule is 'the identifier occurs in the file', which is weaker than 'the file cites the work'. The strict count is reported inside A4 so the gap is visible.
caveats.not_an_error_report: A10's remainder is a list of candidates for the catalogue's keeper to judge, not a list of catalogue errors.
caveats.sieve_is_a_lower_bound: A9 measures identifier-shaped strings, not citations. It cannot see a source referred to by title alone.
caveats.state_travels_with_the_number: Both sides are states at a time: this repository at one commit, the catalogue at one fetch. The catalogue is described in the record as changing nightly.
caveats.what_is_checked: Only the arm of the catalogue whose evidence lies in this repository. 138 entries point at a different repository and are outside what can be verified from here.

pin.note: The catalogue side is pinned by content hash, not by an upstream commit; see SOURCES.md for why, and for the fetch times.
